post.summary: Build or refine a concept graph
post.description:
With a `conversationId`, reads that event's transcript and group chat and writes a ConceptGraphArtifact for it. With a `topicId`, folds every conversation in the series into one topic-scoped graph — which is also how a series predating this feature gets backfilled.
Both run automatically when a conversation with the Concept Cartographer agent stops: the event gets its own graph, and the topic's graph is refined with it. A series unfolds over time, so the topic graph accumulates a version per event rather than being rebuilt, and the sequence of versions records how the series' understanding developed. Concepts keep stable ids across versions, so two can be diffed.
Safe to re-run, and re-running is how a poor extraction gets redone: the second run appends a new version to the existing graph rather than replacing it or creating a duplicate, so both extractions stay readable and comparable.
An ordinary re-run of a topic still folds the graph's current version in as a source, which means a concept already folded away by the size cap stays folded even after raising it. `reset` (topicId only) skips that: it recomputes the whole series from its raw transcripts alone, ignoring the current graph entirely. It still only ever appends a new version, so the pre-reset graph is never lost — it's just no longer what the new one was built from. Costs a full backfill every time, so this is an operator escape hatch, not something to reach for routinely.
The event is treated as running under the Chatham House Rule. Nothing in the output names or otherwise identifies anyone who took part, and statements are paraphrased — a verbatim quotation survives only inside quotation marks and only when it identifies no one.
Registered ahead of `/artifacts/{artifactId}` so `generate` is not read as an id.

conversationId.description: The finished conversation to map. Mutually exclusive with topicId.

topicId.description: The series to refine, folding in every conversation under it. Mutually exclusive with conversationId.

reset.description: Only valid alongside topicId. Recomputes the series graph from its raw transcripts alone, ignoring the current version, so a concept already folded away by a since-raised CONCEPT_CAP is reconsidered rather than staying folded. The pre-reset graph is kept as the previous version, not overwritten. Not exposed in any client UI — an operator action, meant to be rare.

200.description: Nothing was written because the record was too thin to map, or nothing survived the safety checks. Not an error.

202.description: The graph was built and written as a version

report.description: What assembly and the Chatham House checks removed

foldedConcepts.description: Concepts consolidated into a related one because the series graph outgrew its size cap — distinct from mergedConcepts, which counts concepts recognised as the same idea rather than consolidated for space.

The passcode a client must present to read the container's artifacts, minting one if the container does not have it yet. Lets an owner recover the key after the create response, and build an artifact link before the first artifact exists.

post.summary: Process webhook event for specified adapter
post.description:
Processes incoming webhook events for various adapters. The adapter type is determined
from the URL path, and the appropriate handler is invoked to process the event.

Supported adapters may include:
- Zoom
- Slack
- Other integration platforms

parameters.name: adapter
parameters.description: The adapter type to process the webhook for

requestBody.description:
Webhook payload data. The structure varies depending on the adapter type.
Each adapter expects different payload formats based on their respective APIs.

schema.description: Dynamic payload structure based on adapter type

ownerIsAdmin.description: Whether the author is an admin right now, not when they posted. Only present in conversations that use real names, so an anonymous poster is never revealed as an admin.

answersPrompt.description: Reference to the Message ID that this message answers (when responding to a prompt)

hidden.description: Present (always true) only when an admin is shown a message that an admin hid, so it can be marked as hidden to everyone else. Never present for non-admins, nor for the message's own author, who keeps seeing it normally. With the `placeholder` hidden-display policy, non-admins instead get a stub of just `id`, `createdAt`, `parentMessage`, `hidden: true` and `body: null`.

HideReason.description: Why an admin hid something. Optional on hide; unhide also accepts short free text.

targetUser.description: The author whose messages were targeted (user id only).

messageIds.description: Ids whose hidden state actually changed, as the REST call returned them.
Concrete ids whose hidden state changed, with hide-all and reply cascades already resolved. Empty when nothing changed.

hidden.description: The state the ids moved to.

funFact.description: LLM-generated fun fact about the pseudonym

alternateName.description: Optional nickname or abbreviation (e.g. "Jon" for "Jonathan Smith")

direct.description: Indicates if this is a direct message channel

agent.description: Agent ID or name for direct message channel

name.description: The channel name. Optional if this is a direct message channel.

count.description: Max number of messages to include in conversation history

timeWindow.description: Time window in seconds for conversation history

channels.description: Array of non-direct channel names to include in history

directMessages.description: Whether to include direct messages in history

minNewMessages.description: Minimum number of new messages before triggering

directMessages.description: Whether to trigger on direct messages

channels.description: Array of channel names to monitor for messages

timerPeriod.description: Timer period in seconds to trigger agent message processing

$ref.description: Dot-notation path into resolved properties (including feature sub-objects)

agents.description: Agents to create when the feature is enabled

default.description: Whether the feature is enabled by default

properties.description: User-configurable sub-properties shown in the form

category.description: Platform area this feature belongs to

slashCommand.description: Slash command text without the leading slash (e.g. "mindmap"). Omit for passive features.

prerequisite.description: Optional setup instruction shown alongside the description (e.g. how to enable the feature).

userControlled.description: Whether the participant can control this feature (toggle or slash command). false = runs automatically.

enabled.description: Whether this feature is active for this conversation. Present in /features responses; absent means fall back to the type's default.

preEventMinutes.description: Minutes before scheduledTime that the preEvent window opens.

draft.description: Server-computed. True until the conversation has a valid Zoom link, name, topic, scheduledTime, and scheduledEndTime; cannot be set directly by clients.

enabled.description: Whether this feature is active for this conversation. Absent means fall back to the type's default.

goals.description: Goal IDs active for this conversation (must match a defined goal file).

conversationContext.description: Optional context hints that shape how agents interpret the conversation.

behaviorPolicy.description: Configures agent tone, verbosity, and channel-specific behavior.

source.description: Whether the resource was added by the conversation creator or by an AI agent.

category.description: required — speaker-assigned background reading; referenced — cited during the talk and surfaced by the librarian; suggested — proactively recommended by the librarian or speaker.

hasPdf.description: True when a PDF file is attached to this resource. The on-disk filename is not exposed.

citation.description: Full formatted citation string. Used verbatim in RAG metadata when provided; falls back to title/authors/year otherwise.

summary.description: AI-generated content summary; populated asynchronously for required readings.

relevanceReason.description: One-line relevance note generated by the librarian agent.

name.description: Short label spoken to trigger it, e.g. "kudos" — matched fuzzily against what's said after the wake word.

body.description: Read aloud verbatim (never summarized/paraphrased) — organizers author ordinary prose/lists; it's split into natural read-aloud segments at speech time, not stored pre-split.

agent.description: Reference to an existing agent on the base conversation. Mutually exclusive with agentType.

agentType.description: Agent type to instantiate as a new agent. Mutually exclusive with agent.

experimentValues.description: Spread into the cloned or created agent to override defaults (e.g. llmTemplates, agentConfig, llmModel).

GraphNodeProvenance.description: Where a node in a concept graph came from. Every field is optional: a graph assembled from a whole event has no single message to point at, while one built live from the transcript can attribute nearly every node.

conversationId.description: Carried even though the artifact knows its own container, because a topic-scoped graph draws on several conversations.

messageId.description: The specific message this node came from

pseudonym.description: Display name of whoever contributed it

pollId.description: The poll this node was seeded or cited from

GraphSession.description: One conversation (session) behind a series concept graph. Carries only what is safe to show every reader: the conversation's id, its position in date order, and the event's own name and date. Never a participant name or pseudonym.

order.description: 1-based position when the sessions are ordered by event date, ascending.

title.description: The conversation's name. Omitted when the conversation could not be loaded.

date.description: Start of the event (its scheduled time when it never started). Omitted when unknown.

GraphConcept.description: An idea or entity in a concept graph.

id.description: Opaque and stable, so renaming a concept is an edit to one node rather than a delete plus a create, and two versions of the graph stay diffable.

origin.description: Id of the GraphOriginPrompt this concept came out of

gloss.description: One plain sentence saying what this concept means in this discussion.
gloss.example: A registry participants check credentials against.

foldedFrom.description: Labels of concepts folded into this one because the series graph outgrew its size cap. Distinct from an ordinary cross-session merge, which leaves no trace here since the two labels really named the same idea — a folded concept was a genuinely distinct idea, consolidated for space, so its label is kept so a reader can still find it.

conversationIds.description: Every conversation this concept came up in — the de-duplicated, order-preserving union of the conversations behind it, kept through same-label merges and size-cap folds. `provenance.conversationId` stays the first of them (where the concept originated). Ids only; resolve them against the payload's `sessions`.

analyticsId.description: Opaque id, safe to send to analytics: the first 16 hex characters of an HMAC-SHA256 of this node's `id`, keyed with a server secret. Unlike `id`, which is derived from discussion text, it reveals nothing about the discussion and cannot be reversed by guessing text. Computed on every read and never stored; absent when the server has no ANALYTICS_ID_SECRET configured. Ignored if sent back on a write. Concepts and origin prompts only, never contributions.

GraphContribution.description: A relationship between concepts, reified as its own node rather than left as an edge. That is what lets one contribution join three or more concepts at once, which a plain edge cannot express — and why concepts never reference each other directly.

kind.description: The relationship's name, and the short label a client renders on the node

statement.description: What the conversation said about this relationship, in a sentence — the hover or side-panel text behind the short `kind` label. Normally a paraphrase; a verbatim quotation appears only inside quotation marks and only when it carries no personally identifying information.
statement.example: Participants argued a trust registry only means anything if verifiers actually check it before accepting a credential.

concepts.description: Ids of the GraphConcepts this relationship joins

origin.description: Id of the GraphOriginPrompt this contribution came out of

GraphOriginPrompt.description: The prompt or question a concept or contribution came out of: the third node kind. Attached by a direct `origin` reference rather than through a contribution, since an origin is attribution rather than a relationship between concepts.

text.example: What has to be trustworthy for a credential to mean anything?

analyticsId.description: Opaque id, safe to send to analytics: the first 16 hex characters of an HMAC-SHA256 of this node's `id`, keyed with a server secret. Unlike `id`, which is derived from discussion text, it reveals nothing about the discussion and cannot be reversed by guessing text. Computed on every read and never stored; absent when the server has no ANALYTICS_ID_SECRET configured. Ignored if sent back on a write. Concepts and origin prompts only, never contributions.

ConceptGraphPayload.description: The version payload of a ConceptGraphArtifact. Every array defaults to empty, so the artifact can be created when an event starts and fill in as it runs. Nothing about layout is stored — position, size and colour are all derived by the client from the graph itself. Ids are unique across all three arrays, every id in `contributions[].concepts` names a concept in this payload, and every `origin` names an origin prompt in it.

sessions.description: Every conversation that contributed to the graph, ordered by event date ascending. Written by a series (topic) graph; omitted on a single-conversation graph, which has only the one session.

ArtifactVersion.description: One immutable revision of an artifact. Versions are append-only: an edit writes a new one rather than changing an existing one, so the full history stays readable.

versionNumber.description: 1-based and strictly increasing per artifact. Not guaranteed contiguous: an append that claims a number and then fails to write leaves it unused.

payload.description: Kind-specific content, whose shape is determined by the artifact's `type`. A DocumentArtifact payload is `{ body: string }`; a ConceptGraphArtifact payload is a ConceptGraphPayload.

example.body: The group converged on three priorities...

createdBy.description: BaseUser ObjectId — the organizer or agent that wrote this version

note.description: Free-text note on what changed, for a history view

Artifact.description: A shared data object that emerges from one or more conversations — a document, a link to an external resource, or a custom data model a client renders its own way. Scoped either to a single conversation or to a whole topic. The artifact's content is the payload of its `currentVersion`; every earlier version is retained and readable through the versions endpoints.

type.description: Which kind of artifact this is, and therefore which renderer a client should use and what shape its version payload has. Serialized from the mongoose discriminator key.

scope.description: Which container this artifact belongs to

topic.description: Always set. For a conversation-scoped artifact this is the conversation's own topic, so a topic listing can include the artifacts of its conversations for the topic owner and administrators.

currentVersion.description: The newest version — populated by the fetch and list endpoints

locked.description: When true no further versions may be appended; the artifact stays readable

tags.name: Artifact
tags.description:
Shared data objects that emerge from one or more conversations. An artifact is scoped either to a single conversation or to a whole topic, and may be built live while the conversation runs or prepared afterwards. Every revision is retained: reads return the latest version by default, and the full history stays available.
Reads are authorized by the container's artifact passcode, passed as the `artifactPasscode` query parameter, so a client can load an artifact for someone who has never signed in. The conversation or topic owner, and administrators, may read without one. The passcode is minted when a container's first artifact is created and returned in that response.

tags.name: OrganizerConfirmation
tags.description: Confirms a Zoom-relayed calendar invite's resolved organizer. Zoom's own Reply-To header is never verified to belong to who it claims, so a conversation created from one stays a draft (and never auto-starts) until the resolved organizer clicks through from their inbox.
